source.title: Same Architecture, Different Capacity: Optimizer-Induced Spectral Scaling Laws

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some equations and figure labels are garbled in the web extraction, but the relevant tables and descriptions are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests the effect of architectural changes on held-out validation perplexity, relevant to V4, using its own training runs rather than the original loss-scaling analyses. Its main spectral-rank results concern a different measure and are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports validation perplexity for attention-head-count and positional-encoding interventions. It does not fit held-out loss or perplexity power laws, extrapolate loss from small runs, or identify compute-optimal parameter/token allocations. Its many spectral-rank-versus-FFN-width results are about representation capacity, not the loss behavior named in V1–V3 or V7; they are summarized under fits_no_version rather than treated as rows for those versions.
record.test_reason: The study's fixed-parameter attention-head and positional-encoding comparisons measure held-out perplexity and test V4. Its normalization-placement experiments also bear on V4 but were omitted from the record. Spectral-rank scaling measures a different construct from the loss laws in V1–V3 and V7.
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate but omits the normalization trainability result. The authors conclude that spectral-capacity scaling belongs to the architecture–optimizer pair: matched validation loss can coexist with different spectral geometry, update rank controls capacity growth, and optimizer choice changes both architectural spectral effects and which normalization configurations train successfully. They do not establish changes to the original loss-law exponents or compute-optimal allocation.
record.recipe_differences: The study varies FFN width and optimizer, measuring spectral effective rank rather than fitting held-out loss scaling laws; its architectural comparisons report validation perplexity but do not reproduce the original loss-law or compute-optimal methods.
record.method_sensitivity: Optimizer, FFN width, attention-head count, and positional encoding affect reported outcomes. The spectral-rank exponents also differ across token-frequency regimes and training duration.

fits_no_version.finding: Aggregate 160M hard-rank exponents range from 0.29 for AdamW to 0.82 for Muon; soft-rank exponents range from 0.66 to 1.01 across optimizers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice changes how FFN width scales representation spectral capacity.

fits_no_version.finding: TAIL hard-rank exponents are 0.44 for AdamW, 1.02 for Muon and 1.04 for NorMuon at 160M; the broad optimizer separation persists at 350M.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Spectral-capacity scaling depends on optimizer and token-frequency regime across the two tested model scales.

fits_no_version.finding: Extended AdamW training reduces aggregate hard-rank exponent from 0.29 to 0.03 while improving perplexity; matched perplexity with low-rank Dion does not yield matched spectral geometry.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Improving or matching validation loss need not preserve or match representation spectral scaling.

fits_no_version.finding: Reducing Dion update-rank fraction from 1/2 to 1/16 reduces TAIL hard-rank exponent from 0.88 to 0.40.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Update rank constrains dominant-mode spectral-capacity growth.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimizer-induced spectral-exponent shifts exceed attention-head intervention shifts in 28 of 30 comparisons; removing RoPE redistributes spectral scaling differently across optimizers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Architectural effects on spectral-capacity scaling interact with optimizer geometry.

record.problems: The paper states that the experiments use single seeds per optimizer–width configuration; the main results cover GPT-style models at 160M and 350M, and the authors note that tests at 1B+ scale would strengthen generality. Some hard-rank fits have low R2. Perplexity tables report no uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted from the 52-row V4 perplexity comparisons. Spectral-rank results are not rows for the listed loss-based versions because they measure a different construct; representative findings are summarized under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: No held-out-loss power-law analysis spanning several orders of magnitude with other resources non-bottlenecking.
No loss extrapolation from small runs to runs orders of magnitude larger.
No fixed-compute optimization of parameter and token allocation.
No fixed-parameter depth-versus-width sweep or broad architecture survey. FFN-width sweeps increase total parameters and cannot independently test shape invariance.
No loss power-law test in other modalities or training regimes.
No downstream-task scaling or prediction from pretraining loss.
No comparison of fitted loss-law exponents or compute-optimal splits across setups or fitting choices; spectral-rank exponents are a different measure.

missing.what: Add fixed-width normalization-placement comparisons from Table 26. PostLN-25/50/75/full perplexities are AdamW at 10^-4: 64.6/65.6/106.7/diverged; AdamW at 3×10^-4: 41.9/diverged/diverged/diverged; Muon: 28.7/30.1/40.9/diverged; NorMuon: 28.7/29.9/32.8/diverged; Dion 1/2: 29.1/31.7/diverged/diverged; Dion 1/16: 30.7/34.7/diverged/diverged. Diverged means perplexity above 1000. Compare normalization placements within each optimizer and learning rate; do not conflate optimizer comparisons with architecture effects.
missing.locator: Appendix I, Table 26 and accompanying trainability discussion.

record.verdict_notes: Perplexity values match the supplied tables. Cross-entropy differences are calculated as log(value/baseline); V4 concerns loss magnitude, not whether an intervention improves perplexity. The record's head-count direction-based limits_scope label is unwarranted. Model-size labels denote the base 4× configuration, with parameter count varying across FFN widths but held fixed within each architectural pair. Single seeds and absent perplexity uncertainty limit precision. No numerical threshold for 'slightly' is specified by V4.

versions.untested_parts: No power-law fit of held-out loss against parameters, tokens, or compute; perplexity tables are presented as loss-level context.
No small-run loss fit or prediction of substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or loss-minimizing parameter/token split.
Tests attention-head count and RoPE removal, not broad ranges of depth, width, or other architectural choices.
No other modalities or training regimes are tested for the claimed loss power law.
No downstream-task performance is evaluated for predictability from scale or pretraining loss.

The paper shows setup-dependent spectral-rank exponents and training-time changes in spectral scaling, but does not test fitting choices or bending in the claimed held-out-loss laws or compute-optimal split.

relationships.condition: 160M base configuration: 12 versus 6 heads, matched FFN width and optimizer, across eight widths and five optimizers.
relationships.reason: P01–P40 show small loss changes: the largest absolute cross-entropy difference is about 0.039 nats; either direction is consistent with V4.
relationships.display_finding: Changing from 12 to 6 heads produced absolute cross-entropy differences of at most about 0.039 nats across the tested widths and optimizers.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: 160M base configuration: 12 versus 6 heads, matched FFN width and optimizer, across eight widths and five optimizers.
source_check.reason: Tables 13–14 show small loss changes across all matched pairs. The largest absolute difference, ln(36.79/35.40), is approximately 0.0385 nats.

relationships.condition: 350M base configuration: RoPE versus NoPE, matched width and optimizer, across four widths and three optimizers.
relationships.reason: P41–P52 show consistently worse NoPE perplexity but only about 0.031–0.063 nats higher cross-entropy, roughly 1–2% of baseline loss.
relationships.display_finding: NoPE consistently increased perplexity, but cross-entropy rose by only 0.031–0.063 nats, roughly 1–2% of baseline loss.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: 350M base configuration: RoPE versus NoPE, matched width and optimizer, across four widths and three optimizers.
source_check.reason: Tables 15–16 show consistently higher NoPE perplexity, corresponding to approximately 0.031–0.063 nats higher loss, about 1–2% of baseline loss.

relationships.condition: 160M, fixed 4× FFN width: increasing partial PostLN fraction under fixed optimizer and learning rate.
relationships.reason: Text-only evidence, Appendix I/Table 26: PostLN-25 to PostLN-75 raises Muon perplexity 28.7→40.9 and AdamW at 10^-4 64.6→106.7; several other configurations diverge, making shape sensitivity training-dependent.
relationships.display_finding: Increasing PostLN from 25% to 75% raised Muon perplexity from 28.7 to 40.9 and AdamW perplexity from 64.6 to 106.7 at learning rate 10^-4, while several other configurations diverged.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: 160M, fixed 4× FFN width: increasing partial PostLN fraction under fixed optimizer and learning rate.
source_check.reason: Appendix I/Table 26 shows sensitivity increasing with PostLN fraction and varying by optimizer: Muon rises from 28.7 to 40.9, AdamW at 10^-4 from 64.6 to 106.7, and several configurations diverge.

relationships.condition: 160M, fixed 4× FFN width: full PostLN under every tested optimizer and learning rate.
relationships.reason: Text-only evidence, Appendix I/Table 26: every full-PostLN run diverges with perplexity above 1000, whereas each optimizer has trainable partial-PostLN configurations.
relationships.display_finding: Every full-PostLN run diverged with perplexity above 1000, while each optimizer had trainable partial-PostLN configurations.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.condition: 160M, fixed 4× FFN width: full PostLN under every tested optimizer and learning rate.
source_check.reason: Appendix I/Table 26 marks every full-PostLN run as diverged, with perplexity above 1000, while each optimizer trains at least some partial-PostLN configurations.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: The study reports its own fixed-parameter head-count, positional-encoding and normalization-placement comparisons with validation perplexity, directly testing V4.

tranche.reason: Controlled architecture interventions with held-out perplexity bear on V4 through a different experimental design; the spectral-rank laws themselves measure a different construct from loss scaling.

source_check.notes: Appendix A.5 specifies single seeds; reported uncertainty concerns spectral measurements and fits, not repeated-run perplexity uncertainty. The 160M/350M labels refer to base 4× FFN configurations; parameter count varies across FFN widths but is preserved within matched architectural comparisons.

reader_labels.condition: tested 12-head versus 6-head GPT-2 160M configurations and RoPE versus NoPE GPT-2 350M configurations
reader_labels.reason: The reported perplexity differences are generally modest in these tested comparisons, although head-count changes improve or worsen results depending on width and optimizer; rows P01–P52.
